questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer:
Not dropping out of my education. 
I was aware that I HAD to spend a semester abroad, but I was not aware it would be so early in the Japans Studies Bachelor (3rd Semester), so I had the choice of dropping out or going to Japan.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was outside the "popular" more famous regions of Japan (ie. Kansai-region; Tokyo-era), but I might have thrived a bit more in Tokyo or Kansai.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was rough. I was not ready to spend a semester abroad, my language skills was not on par, I was placed in a language class too low meaning I fell behind 15 ECTS points and really has no way of catching up.
I felt isolated and alienated, had a rough time eating due to dietary restrictions, didn't get enough sleep due to staying at a dorm full of drunk idiots (and paradoxically you were not allowed to drink at the dorm, so what the fuck?!).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fine, decent, ok, informative.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were well guided etc. English speaking staff on campus which was nice. Very helpful on getting doctors appointments etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: 1 female only dorm, two co-ed dorms, all on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: On-campus cafes, convenience stores nearby, kitchens in the dorms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Bring ear plugs if you need sleep to function and don't stay at the Minato Dorm - its trashy, noisy, messy. Also don't stay at Minato Dorm!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A bit below academic level, I would say.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The langauge teaching was actually really good and helped me becoming a lot more fluent in talking Japanese; there was a great emphasis on talking and drilling in conjugations and grammatical patterns

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comprehensive Japanese A(II) (Grammar, Reading, Writing).
Tandem Learning A(1)
Cultural Exchange between Japan and the West A
Intercultural Communication A

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Tandem Learning is a good way of getting to socialize with Japanese and international students (especially if you are somewhat antisocial/introverted).
Cultural Exchange btw. Japan and the West focused on the subject through different movies and litterature (especially the works of Ryunosuke Akutagawa) - which was actually really interesting!
Intercultural Communication was a bit dense when it came to theory, but actually fairly interesting in the way it sought be very universal in how culture impacts us, as humans, and sought to teach how to be mindful of the cultural gaps between people and cultures.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A few on campus festivals, gyms, sports/culture classes. School organized tours every other weekend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The tours were nice if you wanted to be touristy.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
People should do what they want. 
There was not a lot of extreme rock that caught my attention, but the one show I attended was GREAT and people were super welcoming!
Visit temples and the mountains, go for long strolls, do some shopping. Second hand stores are great in Japan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No - I should have spend more time at death metal shows than on campus; I did not fit in the normcore crowd of 19 years olds.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: All of them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I can't remember. The Ordung Muss Sein mentality in public spaces?

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Minato is a shitty dorm.
2) If you do not eat meat, be prepared to eating alone a lot and do your own cooking.
3) The exchange student-focused staff is very helpful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't focus on academic achievements. Goof off, do your bare minimum, socialize a lot and focus on things you want to do in Japan.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Managing to buy influenza medicine by myself in broken Japanese.
Also, setraline was dirt cheap!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding food to eat. Also socializing. And getting proper sleep. And overcoming culture shock, language barrier and home sickness.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.answer: Yes
